# Pitfalls — why the templates look the way they do

Each item is a way an ABI-check workflow ends up green while checking
nothing, red for a reason unrelated to the PR, or unsafe. Check the finished
workflow against every one.

## Checks that silently check nothing

- **Baseline built differently from the candidate.** Different compiler,
  flags, build type, or `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS` produces a diff full of noise or a
  not-comparable result. Build both sides with identical commands. See
  [baseline and comparability](shared/baseline-and-comparability.md).
- **Wrong headers.** Pointing `header` at `src/` or the repository root pulls
  private declarations into the contract (every internal refactor becomes a
  "break"); pointing it at nothing drops the check to binary-only evidence and
  misses layout and signature changes. Use the installed public header
  directory.
- **`lang` left at `c++` for a C library.** The Action's default is `c++`;
  C headers parsed as C++ can fail or mis-model declarations.
- **No debug info.** A `Release` build without `-g` loses layout evidence the
  comparison would otherwise use. Prefer `RelWithDebInfo` in the check build.
- **Static library only.** A `.a` has no dynamic export table to gate. Build
  shared for the check, or say the project is out of scope.
- **Snapshot asset not named `*.abicheck.json`.** `abi-baseline:
  latest-release` searches for that suffix; `abi-baseline.json` is never
  found. More than one such asset on one release is ambiguous — use explicit
  per-library downloads.
- **Glob or guessed library path.** `build/*.so` can match a versioned
  symlink, a test helper, or nothing. Name the real file.
- **One step for a multi-library project.** Checks one library and implies
  all are covered. Use a matrix with `fail-fast: false`.
- **Gate never enabled.** `fail-on-breaking: 'false'` left in place forever is
  a report, not a gate. Advisory mode needs an explicit exit condition in the
  setup report.

## Checks that fail for the wrong reason

- **No bootstrap for a release baseline.** The newest existing release has no
  snapshot asset, so the first PR fails to fetch one. Backfill it with the
  release workflow's `workflow_dispatch` input.
- **A `paths:` filter on a required check.** When the filter excludes a PR,
  the required check never reports and the PR cannot merge. Use
  `paths-ignore` for documentation only, or skip inside the job.
- **Hand-installed toolchain.** `apt-get install castxml` on an Ubuntu
  runner commonly resolves a CastXML older than abicheck's supported range,
  which abicheck refuses rather than trusting. Let the Action install its
  dependencies (`dependency-source`, default `conda-forge`); use `mode: dump`
  for snapshots instead of a `run:` step calling a pip-installed abicheck.
- **Unpinned toolchain.** `ubuntu-latest` moving to a new image changes the
  compiler under a baseline dumped on the old one. Pin the runner image
  (`ubuntu-24.04`) and note that the baseline should be refreshed when it
  moves. See
  [compiler and build profiles](shared/compiler-and-build-profiles.md).
- **Skipping the check on an intentional-break label.** The break lands on
  the default branch still unaccepted by the baseline, and every later PR
  fails. The label must relax `fail-on-breaking`, never skip the comparison.

## Unsafe workflows

- **`pull_request_target` checking out PR code.** Runs untrusted code with a
  write-capable token and secrets. Use `pull_request`; publish fork results
  through the trusted `workflow_run` split
  ([fork-PR reporting](https://abicheck.github.io/abicheck/use/fork-pr-reporting/)).
- **Broad or missing `permissions:`.** Without a block the job inherits the
  repository default, which may be write-all. Declare `contents: read` at the
  top and grant `pull-requests: write` / `contents: write` per job.
- **Mutable action refs with elevated permissions.** `@main`, or a tag, on a
  job holding `contents: write` or `security-events: write` lets a repointed
  ref run with that token. Pin by commit SHA, tag in a trailing comment.
  `abicheck/abicheck` is pre-1.0 with no floating major tag: pin an exact
  release (`@v0.6.0`) everywhere.

## Repairing an existing check

When the repository already has an ABI check, report what it actually does
before changing it: which baseline, which headers, whether it can fail. Then
fix it in place rather than adding a parallel workflow. Common findings:

- `mode: scan`, `against:`, `audit:`, `estimate:`, `crosscheck:` — retired in
  0.6 and now hard errors; migrate to `mode: compare` per
  [the Action migration notes](https://abicheck.github.io/abicheck/use/github-action/#migrating-from-mode-scan).
  An audit-only step that relied on scan's default gating needs
  `severity-preset: default` to keep gating.
- `continue-on-error: true` on the check step — it can never fail the job.
- A baseline regenerated from the PR's own build on every run (compares the
  candidate with itself): always green. Never "fix" a failing check this way.
- `abi-compliance-checker`/`abidiff` scripts: abicheck can replace them, but
  migrating is a separate decision — see
  [migrating from ABICC](https://abicheck.github.io/abicheck/start/upgrading-to-0.6/#a5-compat-the-abicc-drop-in-is-removed) and
  [from libabigail](https://abicheck.github.io/abicheck/use/from-libabigail/).

## Optional add-ons (offer when relevant)

- **SARIF / Code Scanning:** `format: sarif` + `upload-sarif: 'true'`, which
  requires `security-events: write` — so pin every action in that job by SHA.
  Single-pair compare only.
- **Full report as an artifact:** `extra-args: -o json=abicheck-report.json`,
  then `actions/upload-artifact`, and pass its `artifact-url` output to
  `pr-comment-report-artifact-url`.
- **Fork PR comments:** the trusted `workflow_run` split —
  [fork-PR reporting](https://abicheck.github.io/abicheck/use/fork-pr-reporting/).
- **Many targets/profiles/baseline channels:** the reusable
  `check-project.yml` workflow —
  [which scenario am I](https://abicheck.github.io/abicheck/integration/).
